steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Geological maps show the distribution of rock types at the surface using colours and symbols

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An outcrop is the area where a particular rock unit is exposed at the surface

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Strike is the compass direction of a horizontal line on a dipping surface; dip is the angle and direction the surface slopes

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The V-rule: dipping beds produce V-shaped outcrop patterns in valleys; the V points in the direction of dip for shallow dips

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between strike and dip? | Q: How does the V-rule help determine dip direction from a map? | Q: What is an unconformity and how does it appear on a geological map?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Strike is the compass direction of a horizontal line on a dipping surface. Dip is the angle of maximum slope of the surface, always measured perpendicular to strike, with its own compass direction ind | In a valley, a V-shaped outcrop pattern points in the direction of dip if the dip is moderate (V in valley rule). For horizontal beds the outcrop follows contours. For vertical beds the outcrop is str | An unconformity is a surface where younger rocks rest on eroded older rocks, representing a time gap in deposition. On a map it appears as a geological boundary where the younger formation cuts across

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: V-rule: V in valley points toward dip direction for moderate dips Horizontal beds: outcrop follows contours; Vertical beds: straight lines across topography Unconformity: younger rocks cut across older rock boundaries on a map Cross-sections: always draw topographic profile first, then project boundaries at correct dip angles
